questions.contextText:
Reading Comprehension (Q.46 – Q.50): Read the following passage carefully and answer the
questions that follow.
Wetlands are among the most productive ecosystems on Earth, often described as the 'kidneys of
the landscape' because of their ability to filter pollutants, absorb excess floodwaters, and recharge
groundwater aquifers. In coastal regions like Odisha's Chilika and Bhitarkanika, brackish lagoons
and mangrove wetlands act as natural buffers against cyclonic storm surges while sustaining the
livelihoods of thousands of artisanal fisherfolk. However, rapid coastal urbanization, agricultural
runoff laden with synthetic fertilizers, and unregulated aquaculture have increasingly degraded
these fragile habitats. Conservationists argue that protecting wetlands requires more than legal
notifications; it demands community-led stewardship that aligns ecological restoration with
sustainable local livelihoods.
questions.questionText: Why are wetlands referred to as the 'kidneys of the landscape' in the passage?
options: Because they are shaped like human kidneys
Because they filter pollutants and regulate water systems
Because they are found only in coastal regions
